# Copilot Instructions — FinDoc Agent

## Project
Agentic RAG backend. Java 17, Spring Boot 3.2, PostgreSQL + pgvector, Kafka.

## Rules
- All JPA entities use UUID primary keys generated by uuid_generate_v4()
- All repository queries MUST include tenant_id filter — never return cross-tenant data
- Use Java 17 records for DTOs and request/response objects
- Use RestClient (not WebClient or RestTemplate) for HTTP calls
- Vector similarity uses cosine distance operator <=> not L2 distance <->
- Kafka consumer must check retry count before sending to DLQ topic findoc.ingestion.dlq
- JWT must carry tenant_id and user_id claims — always extract both in filters
- Chunk size: 512 tokens, overlap: 50 tokens
- Agent loop max iterations: 5 — never remove this guard
- Log trace_id and tenant_id in MDC on every request
- Use Lombok for entity boilerplate accessors instead of handwritten getters and setters. Add setters only where controlled mutation is part of the domain contract; do not expose mutable access to identifiers, relationships, or audit fields without a clear need.
- Prioritize implementation correctness and behavior validation first. Once the implementation is correct, add focused unit tests for the class logic, including failure paths and security boundaries.

## Production engineering standards
- Generated code must be production grade: validate inputs, handle failures explicitly, preserve security boundaries, and avoid placeholder implementations in production paths.
- Keep classes and methods focused on one responsibility. Separate controllers, orchestration services, domain logic, persistence, external integrations, and mapping where those concerns differ.
- Use established design patterns when they fit the problem (for example Strategy for tool or intent selection, Factory for provider creation, and Adapter for external APIs). Do not introduce patterns or abstractions without a concrete benefit.
- Prefer small, dependency-injected components with clear interfaces and testable behavior. Avoid god services, hidden global state, duplicated business rules, and unnecessary coupling between layers.
- Database reads must use parameterized queries and tenant-scoped predicates. Select only required columns, use pagination for collections, and avoid N+1 queries and unbounded result sets.
- Design indexes from actual query predicates, joins, sort order, and cardinality. Add and maintain migrations for required indexes; verify important query plans with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` against representative data when practical.
- For vector retrieval, preserve the cosine-distance operator `<=>`, include tenant and document-scope filters, and use the appropriate pgvector index/operator class for the expected query shape.
- Repository and service tests must cover tenant isolation, pagination or limits, failure paths, and any non-trivial query behavior introduced by the change.

## Package structure
com.findoc.config, .controller, .service.auth, .service.document,
.service.embedding, .service.agent, .service.agent.tools,
.messaging, .repository, .entity, .dto.request, .dto.response,
.exception, .util

## Implementation tracking
- After every implementation phase, create or update a Markdown handoff file under `docs/`.
- If work is divided into stories, use one file per story: `docs/story-<number>-<short-name>.md`.
- Each handoff must include the completed work, pending work, validation performed, and the next implementation item.
- Update the relevant handoff file in the same change as the implementation so it remains accurate across sessions.
- Keep `docs/implementation-status.md` as the index of stories/phases and the authoritative starting point for a new session.
